opengwasr replaces ieugwasr as the way R reaches OpenGWAS data. ieugwasr talks to **Legacy OpenGWAS**, the OpenGWAS service in production today, which is being retired. opengwasr talks to the new OpenGWAS API. ieugwasr stays installable, frozen, until Legacy OpenGWAS is retired, so published analyses can still be rerun.

**If you use TwoSampleMR,** you may not need to change your code. `extract_instruments()`, `extract_outcome_data()`, `clump_data()`, `available_outcomes()`, `ld_matrix()` and `add_metadata()` keep working, and call opengwasr underneath once TwoSampleMR switches over. Your numbers will still move, for the reasons in [What changed scientifically](#what-changed). Read that section.

opengwasr is not a drop-in replacement for ieugwasr. Its functions are named after the new API's own terms (Analysis, Association, GWAS Store, LD Store), and they behave differently where the new data differ. Familiar names that quietly behaved differently would be worse.

> **Status.** No code in this vignette runs yet. It fixes how opengwasr will be used, before the functions are written. Each grey output block marked `# illustrative` holds values taken from the development Data API on 21 November 2026. ieugwasr code is shown for comparison only.

## A typical workflow, before and after {#workflow}

With ieugwasr:

```r
library(ieugwasr)
exposure <- tophits("ukb-b-19953")                       # clumped: r2 0.001, 10,000 kb, EUR
outcome <- associations(exposure$rsid, "ebi-a-GCST003116") # LD proxies for missing variants
```

With opengwasr:

```{r workflow, eval = FALSE}
library(opengwasr)
src <- og_api()                                          # reads OPENGWAS_JWT
exposure <- og_tophits(src, "ukb-b-19953")               # clumped in the matching LD Store
outcome <- og_associations(src, exposure$alid, "ebi-a-GCST003116")
table(outcome$association_status)                        # Imputed Associations, labelled
```

```text
# illustrative
ℹ Clumping OGS-00009:ukb-b-19953 in LD Store hgdp1kgp-v2-EUR-k10, matched to its Assigned Ancestry (EUR): r² 0.0319 within 10,000 kb.
Warning messages:
1: 10,655 of the 79,248 top hits of OGS-00009:ukb-b-19953 aren't in LD Store hgdp1kgp-v2-EUR-k10, so they can't be clumped and were left out.
2: OGS-00009:ukb-b-19953 has 1,014 index variants; only the strongest 1,000 were returned.
ℹ Raise `limit` for more.

 imputed observed
      85      911
```

Every call takes a Source first: `og_api()` here. Legacy OpenGWAS identifiers still work where they name one Analysis, but opengwasr returns the new ones (`OGS-00009:ukb-b-19953`, `OGS-00011:GCST003116`). Use those in new code.

## Function by function {#function-map}

Every ieugwasr function that TwoSampleMR calls:

| ieugwasr | Used by TwoSampleMR in | opengwasr | What changed |
|---|---|---|---|
| `get_opengwas_jwt()` | every data function, as `opengwas_jwt =` | `og_api()` | The token is read once, from the same `OPENGWAS_JWT`, and travels with the Source. No function takes a token argument. |
| `legacy_ids(ids)` | `extract_instruments()`, `extract_outcome_data()`, `mv_extract_exposures()` | `og_analyses(src, ids)$id` | Analyses are named `<store_id>:<analysis_id>`. Legacy identifiers are accepted everywhere if they name exactly one Analysis. Unknown ones are an error, not a silent drop. Legacy identifiers whose analysis now has a later release with different numbers (`finn-b-*`) give that later release, with a warning naming it. |
| `gwasinfo()` | `available_outcomes()` | `og_analyses(src)` | Reads the whole catalogue, page by page. Columns differ: `analysis_label` rather than `trait`, `id` in the new form, and `assigned_ancestry`, `stored_effect_scale` and `sample_size_kind` are new. |
| `gwasinfo(id)` | `add_metadata()` | `og_analyses(src, ids)` | Metadata keeps the API's names: `sample_size`, `n_cases` and `n_controls` (Associations carry them as `n`, `ncase` and `ncontrol`). There is no `unit`. `sd` is now `original_sd`, with `original_sd_method` saying how it was obtained. |
| `tophits(id, pval, clump, r2, kb, force_server)` | `extract_instruments()` | `og_tophits(src, analyses, threshold, clump = TRUE, ld = NULL, r2 = NULL, kb = NULL)` | Still clumped by default, but the default thresholds come from the LD Store (r² about 0.03 within 10,000 kb). r² 0.001 within 10,000 kb is refused. The LD Store matches each Analysis's ancestry, not always EUR. `threshold` can be at most 5e-4. `force_server` is gone. |
| `associations(variants, id, proxies, r2, align_alleles, palindromes, maf_threshold)` | `extract_outcome_data()` | `og_associations(src, variants, analyses, observed_only = FALSE)` | No LD proxies: Imputed Associations are included and labelled instead, so `proxies`, `r2`, `align_alleles`, `palindromes` and `maf_threshold` have no equivalent. Variants can be rsIDs or ALIDs. Large queries are split automatically. |
| `ld_clump(dat, clump_kb, clump_r2, clump_p, pop, bfile, plink_bin)` | `clump_data()` | `og_clump(src, data, ld = NULL, r2 = NULL, kb = NULL)` | Ranks by \|z\|, not p. `pop` becomes `ld = "EUR"`, or the LD Store is matched from the Analyses' ancestry. `clump_r2`/`clump_kb` become `r2`/`kb`, defaulting to the LD Store's own. `bfile` and `plink_bin` become `ld = og_plink_reference(path, plink_bin)`. For `clump_p`, filter `data` before clumping. |
| `ld_matrix(variants, with_alleles, pop)` | `ld_matrix()` | `og_ld_matrix(src, variants, ld, fill_below_t_far = FALSE)` | Named by ALID, which carries the alleles, so `with_alleles` is gone. Pairs the LD Store doesn't hold are `NA`, not 0; `fill_below_t_far = TRUE` sets the weakly linked ones to 0 ([missing pairs](ld.html#ld-matrix-fill)). More than 500 variants are split automatically. |
| `ld_reflookup(rsid, pop)` | the help for `clump_data()` and `ld_matrix()` | none | `og_ld_matrix()`, `og_ld_proxies()` and clumping report the variants the LD Store doesn't hold. |
| `fill_n(d)` | `ldsc_h2()`, `ldsc_rg()` | none needed | Every Association already has `n`, `ncase` and `ncontrol`, with `sample_size_kind`. `og_analyses()` has the same counts under the API's names, `sample_size`, `n_cases` and `n_controls`. |
| `afl2_list()`, `infer_ancestry()` | `ldsc_h2()`, `ldsc_rg()` | none | The new API holds no allele-frequency reference data (it answers `501`). To choose LD, the Analysis's Assigned Ancestry replaces inferring it. TwoSampleMR's LDSC functions move over later. |

Other ieugwasr functions:

| ieugwasr | opengwasr | What changed |
|---|---|---|
| `api_status()`, `user()` | `og_status(src)`, `og_user(src)` | `og_user()` reports your allowance. |
| `phewas(variants, pval = 1e-5, batch)` | `og_phewas(src, variant, threshold = 1e-8, releases)` | One variant per call. The default threshold is 1e-8; pass `threshold = 1e-5` for ieugwasr's. `batch` becomes `releases` (GWAS Store ids). |
| `variants_rsid()`, `variants_chrpos(chrpos, radius)` | `og_variants_rsid(src, rsids)`, `og_variants_chrpos(src, positions)` | Return ALIDs from the GWAS Stores' own variant tables, not dbSNP records. Positions are on GRCh38 and exact: there is no `radius`. |
| `ld_clump_local()`, `ld_matrix_local()` | `og_clump()`, `og_ld_matrix()` with `ld = og_plink_reference(path)` | The same functions as for LD Stores. |
| `variants_gene()` | none | The new API has no gene annotation. |

## What changed scientifically {#what-changed}

These are the reasons the same analysis can give different numbers through opengwasr. None of them happens silently. Each is either a documented default or a refusal that tells you what to ask for instead.

### No proxies: Imputed Associations instead {#no-proxies}

ieugwasr's `associations()` asked for an LD proxy by default when an outcome Analysis lacked a variant: a nearby variant in LD, found in European 1000 Genomes data, with its alleles realigned. opengwasr has no proxy lookup. The new Store Releases are Reference-Completed: beside the Associations each source reported, they hold an **Imputed Association** for most variants the source didn't report, built once, consistently, when the GWAS Store was built.

So a missing variant comes back as itself, labelled `association_status == "imputed"`, rather than as a different variant. Imputed Associations are included by default; `observed_only = TRUE` leaves them out. In the example above, 996 of the 1,000 BMI instruments are found in CAD, 85 of them Imputed; with Observed Associations only, 911. Report how many of your outcome Associations were Imputed.

To look up the variants in LD with a given one, as a question about LD rather than a substitute Association, use `og_ld_proxies()` (see [LD proxies](ld.html#ld-proxies)).

```{r no-proxies, eval = FALSE}
observed <- og_associations(src, exposure$alid, "ebi-a-GCST003116", observed_only = TRUE)
nrow(observed)
```

```text
# illustrative
[1] 911
```

### Continuous traits are per SD {#per-sd}

ieugwasr returned effects on whatever scale each source published: per SD for some continuous traits, in natural units (kg/m², mmol/L) for others. opengwasr returns continuous traits **per SD** by default, so effects are comparable across Analyses, and says so in `effect_scale` on every Association. Binary traits are log odds as before.

So MR estimates for a continuous exposure are now per SD of the exposure. For natural units, pass `original_units = TRUE`. opengwasr rescales by the Analysis's recorded phenotype SD, and refuses when there isn't one, including for binary Analyses stored per SD.

```{r per-sd, eval = FALSE}
og_associations(src, "rs1421085", "OGS-00011:GCST90624700",
                original_units = TRUE)[, c("beta", "se", "effect_scale")]
```

```text
# illustrative
      beta         se effect_scale
 0.4667140 0.01520618     original
```

### Clumping defaults come from the LD Store {#clumping-defaults}

ieugwasr and TwoSampleMR clumped at r² 0.001 within 10,000 kb. The new LD Stores hold every r² only within 3,000 kb. Beyond that, they hold only pairs with r² of at least their `t_far` (about 0.03; 0.063 for AMR), so they can't answer r² 0.001 at 10,000 kb exactly. opengwasr's default is the LD Store's own: within 10,000 kb at its `t_far`. If you ask for 0.001 within 10,000 kb, it refuses, and the error suggests what the LD Store can answer: r² 0.001 within 3,000 kb, or r² of at least `t_far` within 10,000 kb.

Expect different instrument counts from before. Each clumped data frame records the LD Store, r² and window it used (see [clumping provenance](ld.html#clumping-provenance)).

```{r clumping-defaults, eval = FALSE}
unique(exposure[, c("clump_ld", "clump_ld_choice", "clump_r2", "clump_kb")])
```

```text
# illustrative
            clump_ld clump_ld_choice   clump_r2 clump_kb
 hgdp1kgp-v2-EUR-k10         matched 0.03186544    10000
```

### The LD Store matches the Analysis's ancestry {#ld-by-ancestry}

ieugwasr clumped against European LD unless you set `pop`. opengwasr clumps each Analysis in the LD Store of its Assigned Ancestry, inferred from the Analysis's allele frequencies. An Analysis with no confident ancestry (Unassigned), or a set of Analyses whose ancestries differ, is refused unless you choose the LD with `ld`. There is no fallback to European LD.

```{r ld-by-ancestry, eval = FALSE}
og_ld_stores(src)[, c("ld_store", "ancestry", "t_far")]
```

```text
# illustrative
            ld_store ancestry      t_far
 hgdp1kgp-v2-EUR-k10      EUR 0.03186544
 hgdp1kgp-v2-AFR-k10      AFR 0.03490787
 hgdp1kgp-v2-EAS-k10      EAS 0.02922861
 hgdp1kgp-v2-SAS-k10      SAS 0.03152799
 hgdp1kgp-v2-AMR-k10      AMR 0.06315152
```

### Variants are ALIDs on GRCh38 {#alids}

Legacy OpenGWAS identified variants by rsID, with GRCh37 positions. The new GWAS Stores identify them by **ALID**, `chromosome:position:A1:A2` on GRCh38, with `A1` the effect allele ([ALIDs](opengwasr.html#alids) explains them in full). Every Association has both `alid` and `rsid`. opengwasr accepts either, translates rsIDs for you, and returns every ALID an rsID matches rather than choosing one. `rs1421085`, for example, matches two ALIDs in OGS-00011. `position` values are GRCh38, so they differ from the ones in old outputs. PLINK References, usually GRCh37, are matched by rsID.

```{r alids, eval = FALSE}
og_variants_rsid(src, "rs1421085", releases = "OGS-00011")[, c("rsid", "alid")]
```

```text
# illustrative
      rsid            alid
 rs1421085 16:53767042:A:G
 rs1421085 16:53767042:C:T
```

### `beta` and `pval` are computed for you {#derived-beta-pval}

The new API stores `z` and `se`, not `beta`. opengwasr adds `beta` = `z * se` to every Association, and `pval` computed from the p-value the API sends. When |z| is above about 38.5, `pval` underflows to 0, the limit of R's numbers, while `z` stays exact. Column names follow the new API (`effect_allele`, `other_allele`, `chromosome`); TwoSampleMR maps them to its own.

```{r derived-beta-pval, eval = FALSE}
head(exposure[, c("rsid", "z", "se", "beta", "pval")], 2)
```

```text
# illustrative
       rsid        z         se        beta          pval
 rs56094641 -36.4907 0.00201634 -0.07357775 1.555977e-291
  rs6567160  23.1299 0.00233775  0.05407187 2.317582e-118
```
